items.title: 能源部称达普大坝完全安全
items.titleEn: Dhap Dam remains fully safe, says energy ministry
items.status: DeepSeek 正文分析 · 待 Codex 核验
items.statusEn: DeepSeek article analysis · pending Codex review
items.summary: 《加德满都邮报》报道，能源、水资源与灌溉部于周六表示，位于加德满都戈卡尔内什沃市第1区的达普大坝“完全安全”。报道称，该表态是在季风强降雨后外界对大坝状况产生疑虑之际作出的。纳格马蒂与达普大坝项目称，大坝及主要结构处于安全状态，并发布视频表示数日前在大坝区域发现的风险已得到处理。项目方称，9月9日鞍形坝-1附近路边发生滑坡后，自当晚起持续以约每秒400升的流量泄水，水位下降2.38米至2084.80米，约35%的蓄水已安全排出。项目方称正常水位为2087.14米，若降雨使水位超过该高度，水将自动从溢洪道流出。项目方还表示正在加快排水、护岸与应急管理工作，并呼吁公众不要恐慌、仅依据官方信息。以上均为项目方与官方说法，本条目未独立核实。
items.summaryEn: The Kathmandu Post reported that the Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation said on Saturday that Dhap Dam in Gokarneshwar Municipality-1, Kathmandu, remains fully safe, after concerns over the reservoir following heavy monsoon rains. The Nagmati and Dhap Dam Project said the dam and its main structures were in a safe condition and released a video stating that risk observed in the dam area several days earlier had been fully addressed. The project said that after a landslide along the roadside near Saddle Dam-1 on September 9, about 400 litres per second has been released since that evening; the water level fell 2.38 metres to 2,084.80 metres, with about 35 percent of stored water safely discharged. It said the normal level is 2,087.14 metres and excess water would flow out through the spillway. The project said it was expediting drainage, embankment protection and emergency management measures, and urged the public not to panic and to rely only on official information. These are official and project claims, not independently verified here.
items.analysis: 若官方说法成立，加德满都谷地旱季供水的主要调蓄设施目前未出现迫在眉睫的风险，短期内不太可能因该坝发生下游突发性洪水；但报道依据的是能源部与项目方的声明和自述监测，属单一来源，尚无独立水文或工程核验。对客户而言，直接影响有限，主要体现为谷地供水稳定性预期与公众风险感知，若后续降雨或滑坡使泄水与排水措施承压，可能出现水压波动或临时供水中断，需关注官方通告。下一步应核实：项目技术团队的水位、入库流量与泄流原始监测记录，鞍形坝-1附近滑坡体的处置与护岸工程进度，以及溢洪道在正常水位以上的实际运行测试结果。证据缺口包括：无独立机构复核、无第三方对坝体结构的评估、泄水措施持续时间与终止条件未明确，也不清楚该坝与供水服务的具体衔接安排。
items.analysisEn: If the official account holds, the main storage facility for Kathmandu Valley dry-season water supply currently faces no imminent risk, and a sudden downstream flood from this dam in the near term appears unlikely. However, the report rests on ministry and project statements and self-reported monitoring, a single source with no independent hydrological or engineering verification. Customer impact is limited: mainly expectations about valley water-supply stability and public risk perception; if rainfall or landslides stress the release and drainage measures, there could be pressure fluctuations or temporary service interruptions, so official notices matter. Next verification steps: obtain the project technical team's raw records on water level, inflow and outflow; confirm progress on treating the landslide near Saddle Dam-1 and on embankment protection; and check actual spillway operation above the normal level. Evidence gaps: no independent body has reviewed the findings, no third-party structural assessment is cited, the duration and end conditions of the release measures are unspecified, and how the dam connects to specific water services is unclear.
